_comment: The hand-written half. Edit this daily; fetch-data.mjs merges it with FRED and never overwrites it.
summary: The US hadn't attacked Iran in over a month. That ended on Tuesday. Oil prices are back up, or better yet, not going down. Expect inflation expectations to continue increasing, causing the treasury yields to not simmer down. Warsh might (should) hike. Bessent's hands are tied, trying to conduct monetary policy with a fiscal toolbox. Current debt is not sustainable longterm. AI Capex helping economic growth, but lots of data center roadblocks (energy grid + returns). OpenAI just released GPT-6 Astra, so the buildout is shipping something. AI to AGI, maybe. Stagflation on the horizon? Oh, and Vance just said the Fed should cut rates, the Vice President of the United States. Only thing I'll say, grab your popcorn for Sep 16.
_stance_note: fed.stance drives the bird on the Federal Reserve: hawkish | dovish | neutral
_ai_note: Hand-entered - no FRED series covers company capex. The sentence shown lives in COPY.ai in index.html.
_fed_note: lastMove 0 means the FOMC held. Use -0.25 / +0.25 only for an actual move. Hand-entered - nothing validates this.
_oil_note: Optional daily override. Set asOf to the date you read them and fill wti/brent. Used only while newer than FRED's print - if you stop updating, it falls back to FRED automatically rather than showing an ever-staler number.
_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only - alert turns the figure rust.
author: A.M.
_author_note: Shown under the read, so the opinion is signed and separable from the sourced data.
_credit_note: Shown bottom-left on the world. 'author' (A.M.) signs the read; this names the maker.
_watch_note: Set key:true on the one event that matters most; the lighthouse names it and lights its lamp.
